issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as type double, while the UML also specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns int. The solution implementation (and the usual expected student implementation) uses int for the student-count attributes. This creates both an inner-artifact contradiction within the problem statement (attributes typed double but total returned as int) and a cross-artifact type mismatch between the problem UML and the solution code. Students may be confused whether to implement the student counts as double or int and whether getTotalNumberOfStudents should return int or double.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the types for student counts across the specification, template, and solution. Either: (A) Change the UML in the problem statement to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int to match the solution and getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int; or (B) if doubles are intended, change the solution and template attributes to double and adjust getTotalNumberOfStudents() (and any other affected methods) to return double (or document an explicit cast to int). Prefer option A if integer student counts are intended.
